scope: src/main.js lines 34950-38080 — footsteps, takedown, dodge, death cam, last stand, B01 megaplex authored zones, reinforcement spawns (plus adjacent context 36268-36279, 35934-35940, 37196-37232, 37992-38217, and cross-refs to _applyShadowQuality @23423, buildLevel shadowCasters @3168, encounter director gating @41617, campaignEncounters.js b01_alarm_pair)

findings.title: Building 1 (the opening level) directional key light never casts shadows — flat lighting
findings.description: In buildMegaplexB01Map the directional 'key' light is fully configured with a 2048 shadow map and shadow camera frustum, but key.castShadow is hard-set to false (line 37992) and the light is only pushed into localObjects/ceilingLights — never into the local shadowCasters array (declared empty at 37733 and returned empty-ish at 38207). _applyShadowQuality (line 23431-23435) only re-enables castShadow on lights present in levelData.shadowCasters, so the key light stays castShadow=false forever. Every OTHER building gets sun shadows: buildLevel declares `let shadowCasters=[key]` (line 3168) and the custom-map builder does `shadowCasters.push(key)` (line 38319). B01 — which EVERY player loads first (startBuilding line ~35396 hard-routes G.building===1 to buildMegaplexB01Map) — is the only level with no directional shadows. The configured shadow camera/mapSize on key is also dead code.
findings.evidence: key.castShadow=false; ... key.shadow.mapSize.set(2048,2048); key.shadow.camera.left=-75; ... scene.add(key);scene.add(key.target); localObjects.push(key,key.target);ceilingLights.push(key);  // never: shadowCasters.push(key)
findings.fix: Either (a) set key.castShadow=true and add `shadowCasters.push(key);` right after `localObjects.push(key,key.target);` (line 37997) so _applyShadowQuality manages it like every other level, or (b) just push key into shadowCasters and leave castShadow alone — _applyShadowQuality will set it from SETTINGS.shadowQuality. Lowest-risk: change `shadowCasters=[]` at 37733 to be populated by adding `shadowCasters.push(key);` after the key light is created. The shadow camera is already sized for the megaplex bounds (±75 / ±135), so no extra tuning needed.
findings.risk: Enabling a 2048 directional shadow on a 114x220 level adds one shadow pass; on 'low' quality _applyShadowQuality already disables it, so perf-safe. Validate the static probes / vite build stay green (no API change). Watch shadow acne on the large floor — bias may need a nudge, but default PCFSoft is usually fine.

findings.title: Death cam freezes (no camera motion) when player dies with no alive enemy nearby
findings.description: startDeathCam picks the nearest ALIVE enemy as the camera target. If none is alive (died to own grenade, environmental damage, or a bullet still in flight after the last enemy died), `best` stays null and DEATHCAM.killerPos is never set. updateDeathCam returns immediately every frame because of `if(!DEATHCAM.active||!DEATHCAM.killerPos)return;` (line 37111), so the camera just sits frozen at the moment of death for the full 1.7s before the defeat screen — reads as a hard freeze / broken death, not a cinematic. Secondarily, startDeathCam never resets DEATHCAM.killerPos to null first, so a stale killerPos from a previous death can leak into a later death where no enemy is found, aiming the cam at a wrong/old world position.
findings.evidence:
let best=null,bestD=999; ... if(best){DEATHCAM.killerPos=best.group.position.clone(); ...}  // killerPos left as-is (null or stale) when best is null
function updateDeathCam(dt){ if(!DEATHCAM.active||!DEATHCAM.killerPos)return; ...
findings.fix: At the top of startDeathCam set `DEATHCAM.killerPos=null;`. Then after the search, add a fallback when best is null: `if(!DEATHCAM.killerPos){const f=-Math.sin(P.yaw),fz=-Math.cos(P.yaw);DEATHCAM.killerPos=new THREE.Vector3(P.pos.x+f*2.2,WT,P.pos.z+fz*2.2);DEATHCAM.distance=2.2;}` so the cam always has a target (pulls back to a generic over-the-shoulder of the corpse) and never freezes.
findings.risk: Purely additive; only changes behavior in the previously-broken no-enemy case. No save-compat impact.

findings.title: Last Stand stores previous weapon but never restores it on revive — player stuck on pistol
findings.description: When the player enters Last Stand, takeDamage saves the outgoing weapon (`const prev=pl.weaponIdx;pl._lastStandPrevWeapon=prev;` line 37200) and force-switches to the pistol via switchWeapon(1). tickLastStand reviving the player (line 37219-37224) sets hp=25 and _inLastStand=false but NEVER reads _lastStandPrevWeapon — so the player is permanently demoted to the pistol after surviving a Last Stand, even if they were carrying a rifle/shotgun. _lastStandPrevWeapon is a dead write (grep confirms it is written only at 37200 and read nowhere).
findings.evidence: const prev=pl.weaponIdx;pl._lastStandPrevWeapon=prev; switchWeapon(1);  // revive path: P._inLastStand=false;P.hp=25; ... // never: switchWeapon(P._lastStandPrevWeapon)
findings.fix: In tickLastStand's revive branch (right after `P.hp=25;`, line 37222) add: `if(typeof P._lastStandPrevWeapon==='number'&&P._lastStandPrevWeapon!==P.weaponIdx)switchWeapon(P._lastStandPrevWeapon,true);P._lastStandPrevWeapon=undefined;`. Guard with isPlayableWeaponIdx if you want to be defensive about a since-dropped weapon.
findings.risk: Low. switchWeapon already normalizes idx and no-ops if dead/melee-out. Restoring at revive (player alive again) is safe. Keep the force=true so the swap actually plays.

findings.title: extraFocus level-5 unlock adds 0.0 — does literally nothing
findings.description: applyUnlocks grants startCredits/startHeal/startGrenade meaningfully, but `if(u.extraFocus)P.focus=Math.min(1,(P.focus||1)+0.0)` adds 0.0, so the 'extraFocus' unlock earned at Operator Level 5 (saveProgress line 35926) has zero effect. The unlock is surfaced to the player as a reward but is a no-op.
findings.fix: Decide the intended effect. If extra starting focus, change to a real value e.g. `P.focus=Math.min(1.25,(P.focus||0)+0.25)` (requires focus to allow >1 elsewhere) OR if it should raise the focus cap, set a P.focusMax field and read it. Cheapest meaningful fix: `if(u.extraFocus)P.focus=Math.min(1,(P.focus||0)+0.20);` so it tops up focus at building start.
findings.risk: Low; only affects a derived meter at building start. Confirm nothing clamps focus to exactly the old value immediately after applyUnlocks.

findings.title: Combo HUD fill divisor hardcoded to 4.8 but body-kill combo timer is 4.35 — bar never reads full
findings.description: comboKill sets P.combo.timer to 4.8 for headshots but 4.35 for body kills (line 35988). comboTick computes the combo bar width as `P.combo.timer/4.8*100` unconditionally (line 36275). After a body-shot kill the bar maxes out at ~90.6% and visibly never fills to 100%, an inconsistency a player can notice on every non-headshot combo refresh.
findings.fix: Track the window length on the combo object: in comboKill set `P.combo.window=isHead?4.8:4.35;` and in comboTick divide by `(P.combo.window||4.8)`. Alternatively normalize both timers to 4.8 if the shorter body-kill window is unintentional.

findings.title: Dodge roll i-frames (450ms) are shorter than the roll duration (500ms)
findings.description: DODGE.dur=.50 (500ms) but DODGE.iframeUntil is set to performance.now()+450 in tryDodge. takeDamage only grants invulnerability while `now<DODGE.iframeUntil`, so the final ~50ms of the visible roll is vulnerable. The perk description ('dodge with i-frames') implies the whole roll is protected. Minor but can produce 'I rolled and still got hit at the end of the roll' moments.
findings.fix: Set iframeUntil to cover the roll: `DODGE.iframeUntil=performance.now()+Math.round(DODGE.dur*1000)+60;` (a small recovery buffer), or intentionally keep a vulnerable recovery tail and document it. Lowest risk: `+500`.
findings.risk: Slightly more generous dodge; balance-only. No state/save impact.

findings.title: B01 alarm-pair reinforcement spawn is unreachable in the shipping B01 (megaplex) level
findings.description: _spawnCampaignReinforcement -> _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements is only invoked from the reinforcement-drain loop (main.js 41638-41648), which is gated by `G.encounterDirector && hasEnc(encounterDef) && authCE`. But B01 always uses buildMegaplexB01Map, which returns disableEncounterDirector:true, encounterDef:null and spawnDoors:[] — so _syncEncounterDirectorFromLevel sets G.encounterDirector=null (line 6050-6052) and the drain loop never runs for B01. Even if it were reached, _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements reads G.levelData.spawnDoors (empty for megaplex) and returns immediately at `if(!z0.length)return;` (line 35164), so it would never spawn the pair nor show the 'WIDE ALERT' toast. The b01_alarm_pair squad authored in campaignEncounters.js (lines 428, 552) and its story cue thus never fire in the live game.
findings.evidence: function _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements(...){ ... const doors=(G.levelData&&G.levelData.spawnDoors)||[]; const z0=doors.filter(d=>d.zoneId===0); if(!z0.length)return; ...}  // B01 megaplex returns spawnDoors:[] and disableEncounterDirector:true
findings.fix: Two options: (1) If alarm reinforcements should fire in B01, give buildMegaplexB01Map a small set of zone-0 spawnDoors (with ax/az/inwardX/inwardZ) and wire a megaplex-specific reinforcement trigger (since the encounter director is disabled), or (2) accept it as intentionally retired and delete the unreachable _spawnB01AlarmReinforcements + the b01_alarm_pair authoring to remove the contradiction. Recommend confirming design intent before touching campaignEncounters.js.
findings.risk: Option 1 changes B01 difficulty/feel and needs spawn-door geometry; option 2 is data deletion that could affect tests/probes referencing b01_alarm_pair. Verify the 32 static probes after either.

findings.title: Dark-room setpiece dims ceiling lights by *0.25 but setpieceEnd never restores intensity
findings.description: The 'dark' setpiece multiplies every ceilingLight intensity by 0.25 (line 36087) and adds a flashlight. setpieceEnd (line 36253) removes the flashlight and hostages but does NOT restore the dimmed ceiling-light intensities. In practice this is masked because setpieceEnd runs at the next startBuilding where the whole level (and its light objects) is rebuilt fresh — so the dim never visibly carries over. It is still a latent leak/desync: if a 'dark' setpiece is ever ended mid-building, or the same levelData/ceilingLights array is reused, the lights stay at 25% permanently.
findings.evidence: if(G.levelData&&G.levelData.ceilingLights){for(const L of G.levelData.ceilingLights){L.intensity*=.25;}}  // setpieceEnd: no inverse restore
findings.fix: Before dimming, cache the base intensity per light (`L.userData._setpieceBaseInt=L.intensity;`) and in setpieceEnd restore: `if(SETPIECE.kind was dark) for(L of ceilingLights) if(L.userData._setpieceBaseInt!=null){L.intensity=L.userData._setpieceBaseInt;delete L.userData._setpieceBaseInt;}`. Capture SETPIECE.kind before nulling it at the top of setpieceEnd.
findings.risk: Low; only matters in the (currently nonexistent) mid-building setpiece-end path. Avoids a future bug if setpiece lifetime changes.

findings.title: _finishTakedownImpact schedules checkZoneClears via setTimeout that can run after building transition
findings.description: _finishTakedownImpact ends with `setTimeout(()=>checkZoneClears(),90)`. checkZoneClears reads G.enemyMgr/G.zoneClears/G.exitUnlocked. If the takedown finishes within ~90ms of an exit/advance (e.g. the takedown WAS the final kill and the player advances), this deferred call can run mid-transition and operate on a partially-reset G state. checkZoneClears guards with `if(!G.enemyMgr||!G.zoneClears||G.exitUnlocked)return;` so it is mostly safe, but it can still re-fire onZoneCleared/awardBuildingMoney edge effects if exitUnlocked hasn't been set yet at the 90ms mark.
findings.fix: Either call checkZoneClears() synchronously at the end of the impact (the 90ms delay buys nothing functional since the kill/_list removal already happened via takeDamage(9999)), or add a guard `if(!TAKEDOWN.active&&G.started&&!P.dead)checkZoneClears();` inside the timeout. Lowest risk: call it synchronously.
findings.risk: Very low; checkZoneClears is idempotent-ish via its guards. Synchronous call removes a 90ms latency on the ROOM/BUILDING CLEAR beat after an execution (slight feel improvement).
